During my first visit, he advised me to take an X-ray, which I did at his hospital after paying consultation and X-ray charges. The X-ray was normal. To further identify the issue, he then suggested an MRI and specifically gave me a slip and contact number of a particular MRI centre (Pulse), asking me to inform him once the report was ready.
When I contacted that centre, the cost quoted was ₹5000. I checked with Aarthi Scan Centre for the same MRI, where the cost was ₹3800, so I chose Aarthi Scan and completed my MRI there. I sent the report to the number provided by the doctor, but there was no response. Assuming the doctor might be busy, I went directly to the hospital.

When I met the doctor, instead of discussing my foot problem, he focused mainly on why I took the MRI at Aarthi Scan. After briefly looking at the report, he said it was “not clear” and that he could not give treatment, and then suggested another doctor. He also said that if that doctor advised a repeat MRI, it must be done only at Pulse centre.
In my second visit (within 5 days), no examination or treatment was given. The entire discussion was about why MRI should be done at the suggested centre and not elsewhere. For this visit also, I was charged consultation fees.
My concern is simple: if outside MRI reports are not acceptable, this should be clearly informed to patients during the first visit itself. This would save patients’ time, money, and mental stress. I paid consultation fees twice and X-ray charges, yet received no treatment or proper discussion about my actual foot condition.
With the same MRI report, I consulted another doctor (not the one suggested here), and treatment was started immediately. I am now recovering.
I am sharing this review purely based on my experience, not commenting on the doctor’s medical knowledge, but on the way my case was handled.
